title.en: Three Kingdoms to Northern & Southern Dynasties
title.zh: 三国两晋南北朝：政权分立与民族交融

clips.send: Chang’an (Xi’an), Sui capital. Capital of the Sui. In 581 Yang Jian founded the Sui with Chang’an as capital. In 589 the Sui conquered the Chen dynasty and reunified China.
clips.text: Chang’an (Xi’an) · Sui capital。Capital of the Sui。In 581 Yang Jian founded the Sui with Chang’an as capital.。In 589 the Sui conquered the Chen dynasty and reunified China.

clips.send: In 317 Sima Rui founded the Eastern Jin at Jiankang, while the north entered the Sixteen Kingdoms period. Large numbers of northerners moved south, bringing labour and advanced farming techniques; with good natural conditions and relative peace, the Jiangnan region was developed.
clips.text: In 317 Sima Rui founded the Eastern Jin at Jiankang, while the north entered the Sixteen Kingdoms period. Large numbers of northerners moved south, bringing labour and advanced farming techniques; with good natural conditions and relative peace, the Jiangnan region was developed.

clips.send: Northern Wei later split into Eastern and Western Wei, replaced by Northern Qi and Northern Zhou. In 581 Yang Jian founded the Sui; in 589 Sui conquered Chen and reunified north and south, ending nearly four centuries of division.

clips.send: Late in the Eastern Han, the Yellow Turban uprising broke out in 184. Afterwards local strongmen and officials raised their own armies: Yuan Shao and Cao Cao in the north, the Sun family in Jiangdong, Liu Biao in Jing Province and Liu Zhang in Yi Province.

clips.send: Battle of Chibi (208). Around today’s Chibi, Hubei, Sun Quan + Liu Bei vs Cao Cao. In 208 Cao Cao marched south; the allied armies of Sun Quan and Liu Bei attacked his fleet with fire at Chibi on the Yangtze. Cao Cao retreated north; this laid the foundation for the three kingdoms.

clips.send: The Northern Wei, founded by the Tuoba branch of the Xianbei, unified the Yellow River valley in 439. In 494 Emperor Xiaowen moved the capital from Pingcheng to Luoyang and carried out reforms to adopt Han culture, promoting the blending of the northern peoples.

clips.send: Each kingdom developed: Wei built irrigation and military farms, and the northern economy recovered; Zhuge Liang governed Shu and developed the southwest; in 230 Wu sent Wei Wen with a fleet to Yizhou (today’s Taiwan), strengthening links between the mainland and Taiwan.

clips.send: In 383, at the Battle of the Fei River, the Eastern Jin defeated Former Qin, which had unified the north, with far fewer troops. From 420 the south was ruled in turn by the Song, Qi, Liang and Chen — the Southern Dynasties — all from Jiankang.

clips.send: Wei. In 220 Cao Pi became emperor; capital Luoyang. Wei built irrigation works and military farms (tuntian); the northern economy recovered. Wei conquered Shu in 263.

clips.send: Shu (Han). In 221 Liu Bei became emperor in Chengdu; the state is called Shu. Zhuge Liang governed well and helped develop the southwest.

clips.send: In 200 Cao Cao met Yuan Shao at Guandu. Though outnumbered, Cao Cao raided Wuchao and burned Yuan’s grain — a victory of the few over the many. Afterwards Cao Cao gradually unified the north.

clips.send: Wei conquered Shu in 263; in 266 Sima Yan founded the Western Jin at Luoyang, and in 280 it conquered Wu, ending the division. Meanwhile the Xiongnu, Xianbei, Jie, Di and Qiang moved inward in large numbers and lived among the Han. After the War of the Eight Princes, the Western Jin fell in 316.

clips.send: Luoyang. Capital of Wei, Western Jin and (after 494) Northern Wei. Cao Pi made Luoyang the capital of Wei in 220; the Western Jin kept it. In 494 Emperor Xiaowen moved the Northern Wei capital here from Pingcheng.

clips.send: Jianye / Jiankang (Nanjing). Capital of Wu, Eastern Jin and the Southern Dynasties. Wu’s capital Jianye was renamed Jiankang in the Jin. Eastern Jin and all four Southern Dynasties (Song, Qi, Liang, Chen) ruled from here; it became a great commercial city.

clips.send: Battle of Guandu (200). Near today’s Zhongmou, Henan, Cao Cao vs Yuan Shao. Cao Cao, with a smaller army, burned Yuan Shao’s grain stores at Wuchao and won. A famous victory of the few over the many; it laid the foundation for Cao Cao to unify the north.

clips.send: Wu. In 222 Sun Quan became King of Wu; capital later Jianye (today’s Nanjing). In 230 Wu sent Wei Wen with a fleet to Yizhou (today’s Taiwan). The economy of the Jiangnan region began to develop.

clips.send: Yungang Grottoes. Today: West of Datong, Shanxi. More than 50,000 Buddhist statues are carved into a sandstone cliff near the old Northern Wei capital Pingcheng. The biggest Buddha is about 17 m tall.

clips.send: In 220 Cao Pi became emperor of Wei with its capital at Luoyang. The next year Liu Bei became emperor in Chengdu (the state is called Shu). In 222 Sun Quan became King of Wu, later with its capital at Jianye. The three kingdoms stood like the three legs of a ding.

clips.text: 263年魏灭蜀；266年司马炎建立西晋，定都洛阳；280年西晋灭吴，结束分裂。西晋时匈奴、鲜卑、羯、氐、羌等族大量内迁，与汉族杂居。“八王之乱”后，西晋于316年灭亡。

clips.send: 208年，曹操率大军南下。孙权和刘备组成联军，在长江赤壁一带用火攻大败曹军。曹操退回北方。赤壁之战奠定了三国鼎立的基础。

clips.send: 隋。581年杨坚建立隋朝，589年隋灭陈，南北重归统一。结束了近四百年的分裂局面。

clips.send: 夷洲（今台湾）。230年吴国船队到达。230年孙权派卫温率领万余人的船队到达夷洲。加强了大陆和台湾的联系。

clips.send: 蜀（汉）。221年刘备在成都称帝，国号汉，史称蜀。诸葛亮治蜀，西南地区得到开发。

clips.send: 383年淝水之战，东晋以少胜多打败统一北方的前秦。420年以后，南方先后经历宋、齐、梁、陈四个朝代，史称南朝，都城都在建康。
